svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "An action potential (nerve impulse) arrives at the presynaptic knob, depolarising the presynaptic membrane."], [2.5, "Depolarisation opens voltage-gated calcium ion channels: Ca\u00b2\u207a ions diffuse into the knob down their concentration gradient."], [5, "The rise in Ca\u00b2\u207a makes synaptic vesicles move to the presynaptic membrane and fuse with it (exocytosis), releasing acetylcholine into the synaptic cleft."], [7.5, "Acetylcholine diffuses across the cleft and binds to receptor proteins on the postsynaptic membrane: its shape is complementary to their binding sites."], [10, "Binding opens the receptors\u2019 sodium ion channels. Na\u207a ions diffuse in and depolarise the postsynaptic membrane; if the threshold is reached, an action potential starts in the next neuron."], [13, "Acetylcholinesterase breaks acetylcholine down, so the channels close and the signal stops. The products are reabsorbed into the knob and recycled; Ca\u00b2\u207a is pumped back out."]]
svg.title: A chemical synapse
svg.desc: A chemical synapse between two neurons: the presynaptic knob with mitochondria, synaptic vesicles and calcium ion channels, the synaptic cleft with acetylcholinesterase, and the postsynaptic membrane with receptor proteins that are sodium ion channels.
svg.text: Cholinergic synapse (neurotransmitter: acetylcholine). The cleft is widened for clarity; not to scale.

g.data-info: Carries the action potential (nerve impulse) to the synapse.
The swollen end of the axon. It makes the neurotransmitter and stores it in vesicles.
Membrane of the axon terminal. Vesicles fuse with it to release neurotransmitter by exocytosis.
Release energy (ATP) by aerobic respiration, used to make neurotransmitter, refill vesicles and pump ions.
Small membrane sacs filled with neurotransmitter molecules (here acetylcholine).
Voltage-gated channels in the presynaptic membrane. They open when an action potential arrives, so Ca²⁺ ions diffuse into the knob.
The gap between the two neurons, about 20 nm wide. The neurotransmitter crosses it by diffusion.
The next neuron. Enough depolarisation of its membrane starts a new action potential in it.
Membrane of the next neuron (or muscle cell), containing receptor proteins for the neurotransmitter.
Proteins with a binding site complementary in shape to the neurotransmitter. When acetylcholine binds, the channel opens and Na⁺ ions diffuse in.
Enzyme in the cleft that rapidly breaks acetylcholine down into choline and ethanoate, so the signal stops; the products are reabsorbed and recycled.

g.text: 2 Ca²⁺ channels open; Ca²⁺ diffuses in
4 Acetylcholine diffuses and binds to receptors
